title: Column-zero representatives in a good total resolution
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $K$ be a bicomplex of $R$-modules, with both differentials raising their integer index [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Suppose $K.X(p)$ is zero for $p>0$. Let $T$ be its direct-sum total complex, with the usual signed differential, and let $j:K.X(0)\to T$ be a chain map whose component in each degree $q$ is the inclusion of the summand $(0,q)$. Assume for every $p<-1$ and every integer $q$ that $H^q(K.X(p))\to H^q(K.X(p+1))\to H^q(K.X(p+2))$ is exact, where the maps are induced by the horizontal differentials and homology is cycles modulo boundaries. Then for every integer $n$ the map $H^n(j)$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 09IZ, lemma-good-resolution-gives-qis, proof, second paragraph (finite-support reduction)

proof.text: Put A_i = K.X (-i). Represent a total homology class by a cocycle x. The coproduct of modules is their direct sum, so x has finite support. Positive columns vanish, hence x is supported in A_0 through A_r for some natural number r.

If r > 0, the cocycle equations in columns r and r-1 show that x_r is a vertical cycle whose horizontal image is a vertical boundary. Exactness of the horizontal homology row lifts its class to a class in A_(r+1) in vertical degree n+r. Represent that class by a vertical cycle y; its total degree is n-1.

Subtract the total boundary of y, adjusting by the horizontal unit sign, to turn x_r into a vertical boundary. Choose a primitive t in A_r of vertical degree n+r-1 and subtract its appropriately signed total boundary. This kills x_r; the only other column affected is r-1. Induction on r gives a homologous cocycle supported in column zero.

The final column-zero component is a vertical cycle. Its homology class maps to the original class by j, since the components of j are the specified total inclusions. If r=0, no modification is needed; the zero class is represented by zero.
